subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & evals (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@globexretail.com>, Antonio Pereira <antonio.p@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & evals (EU / APAC)

Hi Elena / Antonio —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clear breakdown of your EU/APAC catalog and the multilingual quality pain points (particularly French/German SLAs for search snippets and Japanese/Korean product descriptions). Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Summary of what we heard:
  - Primary focus: high-precision QA for product descriptions and short-form search snippets in FR/DE/ES/JA/KO.
  - Current issues: inconsistent translations, hallucinations on inventory-sensitive prompts, and timezone-bound batch processing for APAC.
  - Success criteria: >90% factuality for product attributes, <5% critical hallucinations, latency <300ms P50 for snippet generation.

- Initial model recommendations (based on your latency & cost targets):
  1) Redwood-Chat-27B (quantized) — strong instruction-following and cost-balanced for mixed-length outputs.
  2) Llama-3-13B-instruct (4-bit quant) — lower-cost candidate; may require prompt engineering for rare-language coverage.
  3) Mistral-Instruct-7B (fine-tuned) — good for short, high-throughput snippet generation (APAC bursts).

- What we’ll evaluate in the pilot:
  - Benchmarks for FR/DE/ES/JA/KO: factuality, hallucination rate, localization (date/currency/units), and token-efficiency.
  - Prompt set: seed prompts (attached) + your sample corpus (you mentioned ~12k product descriptions).
  - Evaluation plan: automated metrics + human spot checks (20 per language for critical flows).

Attachments: globex_multilingual_benchmarks_v1.pdf (baseline metrics), prompt_set_globex.csv (seed prompts).

Next steps:
  1) We’ll run a focused 48–72 hour priority eval on FR/ES/JA (these are your highest-risk locales) and share a quality regression risk matrix.
  2) Neha will detail the technical eval plan and required assets.
  3) If the pilot looks good, we can propose a Dedicated pool for peak APAC bursts to meet latency targets.

Can you confirm the sample corpus delivery (S3 link or Drive) and if the 48–72 hour eval window starting Monday, Apr 12 works for you?

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few things from our side: 

- Corpus delivery: we can share an anonymized S3 bucket with 12,400 product descriptions + 3 sample storefront queries per locale by end of day Monday. I’ll send access.
- Priority locales: FR/DE/ES for EU; JA/KO for APAC. If you have to prioritize, start with FR/ES/JA.
- Quality/regression ask: we need a short document that explains how you detect and mitigate quality regressions between model variants (we’ve had regressions after tuning in past vendors). Can your eval include a ’regression risk’ column per model?

Also — procurement will want a rough cost estimate for a 30-day pilot (including Dedicated burst hours if needed). Antonio will lead procurement questions; I’m looping him in.

Appreciate the attachments — will review.

Best,
Elena

Subject: RE: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & evals (EU / APAC) — technical eval plan

Hi Elena / team,

Following up with a proposed technical evaluation plan so you can see what we’ll run in the 48–72h window. High-level: automated pass/fail + human spot checks, language-specific edge tests, and a regression-risk scoring rubric.

Proposed plan (48–72 hour run):
1) Ingest: consume your anonymized S3 corpus (metadata preserved: locale, product_type).
2) Seed prompts: use prompt_set_globex.csv (attached). We’ll expand by perturbations (+ synonyms, unit conversions).
3) Models to evaluate: Redwood-Chat-27B (quant), Llama-3-13B-instruct (4-bit), Mistral-Instruct-7B-finetuned.
4) Metrics: factuality (precision/recall on attribute extraction), hallucination rate (false attribute insertion), localization accuracy (dates/currencies), latency P50/P95, token cost per output.
5) Regression risk: for each model we compute delta vs baseline across metrics; we’ll flag any metric with >5% negative delta as 'high risk'. We’ll include a short remediation suggestion (prompt tweak, temperature clamp, or fallback to higher-capacity model).
6) Human QA: 20 samples per language reviewed for critical flows (descriptions, inventory-dependent attributes).

Deliverables after run:
- CSV with per-sample predictions and automated labels (used for quick triage).
- Regression risk matrix (per-model, per-locale).
- Recommendation: model + prompt set + estimated Dedicated pool size for APAC bursts.

Attachments: eval_matrix_proposal.xlsx (sheet: metrics & thresholds), prompt_set_globex.csv.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the S3 path and IAM role OR a Drive share?
- Any specific disallowed behaviors (e.g., no auto-creation of SKUs, no price inference) to include in the safety filters?

If you confirm access by Monday 6 AM PDT, we can queue the eval to start Mon 8 AM PDT and have a first-pass report by Tue EOD.

—
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

Thanks — confirming the proposed timeline works. A couple procurement / pilot questions before we proceed: 

1) Cost: can you provide a ballpark cost for the 48–72h eval (compute + S3 io) and a separate estimate for a 30-day pilot that includes Dedicated APAC burst (approx 8 hours/day peak for 2 weeks)?
2) Trial terms: are there any limits on tokens processed during the pilot and a standard NDA/data processing addendum we need to sign?
3) SLOs: for the pilot, can you commit to a P50 latency target and escalation path if we see >10% error rates in the critical flows?

We’re happy to move forward once we have those items (procurement will need rough numbers for internal approval). Elena — can you confirm the Tue sync invite once Marissa sends it?
